attractions.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque, Muscat
attractions.desc: One of the few mosques in the Gulf region open to non-Muslim visitors, notable for a prayer hall carpet that was, at the time of its installation, the largest single piece in the world. Its main dome and minarets combine Islamic architectural styles from across the region. Modest dress, including a headscarf for women, is required.

attractions.name: Wahiba Sands
attractions.desc: A sea of orange dunes stretching toward the coast, home to Bedouin communities who still herd camels and goats across the desert. Overnight camps offer dune driving, camel treks, and clear night skies far from city light. It's a manageable day trip from Muscat or an overnight stop en route south.

attractions.name: Wadi Shab
attractions.desc: A canyon of turquoise pools fed by mountain springs, reached by a walk and a short boat crossing before hiking between rock walls to a hidden cave with a waterfall. Swimming through narrow sections of the canyon is part of the appeal. It's one of the most popular wadis for a reason, so early arrival helps avoid crowds.

attractions.name: Jebel Akhdar
attractions.desc: The 'Green Mountain', a high plateau in the Hajar range known for terraced rose and pomegranate farms clinging to the cliffs. Its elevation makes it noticeably cooler than the coast, a welcome break in summer months. Hiking trails wind along old village terraces with sweeping canyon views.

attractions.name: Nizwa Fort & Souq
attractions.desc: A 17th-century circular fort with a commanding tower, once a key defensive point for the interior region. Its Friday goat market and adjoining souq selling silver, dates, and pottery give a strong sense of traditional Omani trade life. It's a common stop en route to Jebel Akhdar.

attractions.name: Musandam Peninsula
attractions.desc: A dramatic exclave separated from the rest of Oman by UAE territory, where steep mountains plunge directly into the fjord-like waters of the Strait of Hormuz. Dhow cruises through the channels here are often compared to Norwegian fjords, complete with dolphin sightings. It requires a separate trip from the main Omani circuit.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Muscat
itinerary.desc: The Grand Mosque, old town corniche, and the Mutrah souq.
itinerary.cost: The Grand Mosque is free to visit (modest dress required); the Mutrah souq itself is free to wander.
itinerary.food: Try shuwa if visiting during a local celebration, or a simpler majboos at a casual restaurant any other time.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Wadi Shab & the coast
itinerary.desc: A canyon hike and swim en route toward the desert.
itinerary.cost: Wadi Shab access is largely free; a small boat ferry across the initial water crossing costs a nominal fee.
itinerary.food: Pack your own snacks and water — this is a hiking day with limited food options along the way.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Wahiba Sands
itinerary.desc: An overnight desert camp with dune driving and camel treks.
itinerary.cost: Desert camp packages with dune driving and camel treks run $80–150 per person, usually including meals.
itinerary.food: A traditional Bedouin-style dinner under the stars is typically included with desert camp stays.

itinerary.label: Days 6–7
itinerary.title: Nizwa & Jebel Akhdar
itinerary.desc: The fort and souq, then up into the cool mountain terraces.
itinerary.cost: Nizwa Fort entry costs a modest fee, a few Omani rial.
itinerary.food: Try Omani halwa at a shop in Nizwa's souq — a genuine local specialty worth bringing home.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Return to Muscat
itinerary.desc: Drive back to the capital for departure.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% is appreciated in restaurants but not obligatory
goodToKnow.safety: One of the safest countries in the Middle East for travelers
goodToKnow.gettingAround: A rental car is the best way to see wadis and the desert independently
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Muscat International Airport (MCT), the country's main gateway

food.name: Shuwa
food.desc: Slow-cooked, spiced lamb or goat traditionally cooked underground for up to two days.

food.name: Omani halwa
food.desc: A dense, sweet dessert made from sugar, ghee, and spices like cardamom and saffron.

food.name: Majboos
food.desc: Spiced rice cooked with meat, similar to biryani, a staple across the Gulf.

food.name: Omani coffee (kahwa)
food.desc: Lightly roasted coffee flavored with cardamom, traditionally served with dates.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Oman?
faq.a: Yes, an e-visa is required for most nationalities, applied for online in advance.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Muscat International (MCT), the country's main gateway.

faq.q: Do I need a 4x4 for this itinerary?
faq.a: Yes, essential for Wahiba Sands and recommended for some wadi approaches — a standard car won't handle the sand or rougher tracks.
Yes, consistently rated one of the safest countries in the Middle East for travelers, with a strong tourism infrastructure.

daysReason: 8 days covers Muscat, Wadi Shab, Wahiba Sands, and Nizwa/Jebel Akhdar without rushing. 5–6 works if you drop one region; 10+ lets you add Salalah in the south, a very different Oman.
visa: An e-Visa is required for most nationalities and should be applied for online in advance — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Grande Mesquita do Sultão Qaboos, Mascate
attractions.desc: Uma das poucas mesquitas do Golfo abertas a visitantes não-muçulmanos, notável por um tapete da sala de oração que, na altura da instalação, era a maior peça única do mundo. A sua cúpula principal e minaretes combinam estilos arquitetónicos islâmicos de toda a região. É exigido vestuário modesto, incluindo lenço de cabeça para mulheres.

attractions.name: Dunas de Wahiba
attractions.desc: Um mar de dunas cor de laranja estendendo-se em direção à costa, lar de comunidades beduínas que ainda pastoreiam camelos e cabras pelo deserto. Acampamentos durante a noite oferecem condução em dunas, passeios de camelo, e céus noturnos límpidos longe da luz da cidade. É uma excursão de um dia razoável desde Mascate ou uma paragem durante a noite a caminho do sul.

attractions.name: Wadi Shab
attractions.desc: Um canyon de piscinas turquesa alimentadas por nascentes de montanha, alcançado por uma caminhada e uma curta travessia de barco antes de percorrer entre paredes rochosas até uma gruta escondida com uma cascata. Nadar através de secções estreitas do canyon faz parte do atrativo. É um dos wadis mais populares por uma razão, por isso chegar cedo ajuda a evitar as multidões.

attractions.name: Jebel Akhdar
attractions.desc: A 'Montanha Verde', um planalto elevado na cordilheira Hajar conhecido pelos terraços de rosas e romãs agarrados às falésias. A sua altitude torna-a notavelmente mais fresca do que a costa, uma pausa bem-vinda nos meses de verão. Trilhos de caminhada serpenteiam ao longo de socalcos de aldeias antigas com vistas amplas sobre o canyon.

attractions.name: Forte e Souq de Nizwa
attractions.desc: Um forte circular do século XVII com uma torre imponente, outrora um ponto defensivo chave para a região interior. O seu mercado de cabras à sexta-feira e o souq adjacente, vendendo prata, tâmaras e cerâmica, dão uma forte noção da vida comercial tradicional omanense. É uma paragem comum a caminho de Jebel Akhdar.

attractions.name: Península de Musandam
attractions.desc: Um enclave dramático separado do resto do Omã por território dos Emirados, onde montanhas íngremes mergulham diretamente nas águas do Estreito de Hormuz. Cruzeiros de dhow pelos canais aqui são muitas vezes comparados aos fiordes noruegueses, completos com avistamentos de golfinhos. Requer uma viagem separada do circuito omanense principal.

itinerary.label: Dia 3

itinerary.label: Dias 6–7

food.name: Shuwa
food.desc: Cordeiro ou cabra especiados e cozinhados lentamente, tradicionalmente debaixo da terra durante até dois dias.

food.name: Halwa omanense
food.desc: Uma sobremesa densa e doce feita de açúcar, ghee e especiarias como cardamomo e açafrão.

food.name: Majboos
food.desc: Arroz especiado cozinhado com carne, semelhante ao biryani, um prato base em todo o Golfo.

food.name: Café omanense (kahwa)
food.desc: Café ligeiramente torrado aromatizado com cardamomo, tradicionalmente servido com tâmaras.
